newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk group sees no big strike, maybe disruption.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk group sees no big strike, maybe disruption.

text.p: A spokesman for the management of Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group said on Tuesday that workers at the company's flagship plant would not carry out a widespread strike, but said some disruptions were possible.

"It is clear that there will be no widespread strike," said Sergei Vetchinin. "Clearly, if people were intending to stage an all-out strike, they would have already done so, because this had been going on since February 1."
He said that a one-hour strike scheduled for March 27 would take place on the same day as a scheduled nationwide protest by various unions across Russia.
"So whatever they (Norilsk workers) do on that day will be less a concrete strike and more a show of solidarity," Vetchinin said.
He said the main plant's strike committee would meet March 14 to discuss strike plans.

Valery Glazkov, head of the main plant's United Trade Union, said earlier on Tuesday that workers at Norilsk Nickel's flagship metals plant, the mining and metallurgical complex, planned a one-hour warning strike on March 27 and a proper strike on April 2 over unpaid wages and holiday packages.
Norilsk complex workers passed a vote of no-confidence in management on February 1.
